Measure whether reduced loop-carried dependence helps on both random and decreasing inputs, after correctness checks.

mission.hypothesis: A six-way scalar unroll tests whether a moderate number of independent minimum/index chains can approach the measured two- and eight-accumulator results while avoiding the overhead that may have hurt three and four accumulators. It may help most on decreasing inputs, where each lane's minimum is repeatedly updated; on random inputs, extra comparisons and the final fold may outweigh reduced loop-carried dependence. Prior measurements are aggregate, so per-pattern outcomes remain to be checked after correctness validation.

retained: Replaced the single-chain scan with a fixed six-way scalar scan using six independent minimum-value and index accumulators.
Folded the six results using signed minimum-value comparison and lowest-index tie-breaking.
Handled inputs smaller than six with a scalar scan and processed any remaining elements scalarly after the fold.
Used no explicit SIMD and no parallel workers.
